title: VPC endpoints (Gateway versus Interface)
hook: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) endpoint lets private subnets reach AWS services without NAT or the public internet. Gateway endpoints are route-table shortcuts for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB; Interface endpoints create Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) for other services via AWS PrivateLink.

blocks.text: VPC endpoints are private front doors to AWS services. Gateway endpoints add an AWS prefix list to your route table for S3 or DynamoDB. Interface endpoints place ENIs in your subnets; DNS can resolve standard service hostnames to those private IPs.

entries.plainDefinition: Route-table target for S3 or DynamoDB traffic on the AWS backbone.
Private ENI in your subnet terminating PrivateLink to an AWS service.
Resource policy limiting which APIs or ARNs are reachable via the endpoint.
entries.example: Allow s3:GetObject only on prod-* buckets.

entries.plainDefinition: Regional service hostname resolves to endpoint ENI private IPs inside the VPC.

blocks.text: NAT gateways bill hourly and per gigabyte. Large S3 pulls from private subnets should use a Gateway endpoint. Interface endpoints keep Secrets Manager, STS, and ECR off the public internet — required for many compliance frameworks.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Name the two types, which services each supports, and the three control planes: route tables, security groups, endpoint policies.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Choose type
items.body: S3/DynamoDB → Gateway. All other AWS services → Interface.

items.title: Gateway setup
items.body: Associate endpoint with route tables. No subnet or SG on the endpoint.

items.title: Interface setup
items.body: Pick one subnet per AZ, attach SG allowing 443 from clients, enable private DNS if desired.

items.title: Harden
items.body: Attach least-privilege endpoint policy in addition to IAM.

diagram.title: Endpoint types
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  EC2[Private EC2] --> RT[Route table]
  RT --> S3[(S3 Gateway endpoint)]
  EC2 -->|443| ENI[Interface ENI]
  ENI --> SM[Secrets Manager]

snippet.label: CLI — S3 Gateway endpoint
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 \
  --route-table-ids rtb-private-a rtb-private-b
snippet.explanation: Injects S3 prefix list routes. No security group parameter.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — Interface endpoint
snippet.code:
SecretsEndpoint:
  Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
  Properties:
    VpcEndpointType: Interface
    ServiceName: !Sub com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.secretsmanager
    PrivateDnsEnabled: true
    SubnetIds: [!Ref PrivateA, !Ref PrivateB]
    SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref EndpointSg]
snippet.explanation: Interface endpoints need subnets and a security group. PrivateDnsEnabled preserves SDK hostnames.

snippet.label: Endpoint policy
snippet.explanation: Restricts data plane even when IAM is broad.

snippet.label: CLI — describe endpoints
snippet.explanation: Verify PrivateDnsEnabled and DnsEntries when SDK calls time out.

blocks.title: Pitfalls
blocks.body: Interface steps for S3. Missing SG on Interface ENI. One route table not associated — partial AZ failure.

blocks.text: Gateway endpoints are prefix routes without ENIs. Interface endpoints bill per-AZ ENI hour plus data processing. How to prove it in production: NAT gateway BytesOutToDestination drops after S3 Gateway adoption; Flow Logs to S3 prefix bypass NAT IPs; dig from bastion confirms private DNS for Interface endpoints.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying endpoints replace security groups. Strong: Gateway = routes; Interface = ENI + SG + endpoint policy. S3/DynamoDB are Gateway-only.

interviewTakeaways: Gateway endpoints = S3 and DynamoDB via route tables; Interface endpoints = ENI PrivateLink for other services.
Interface endpoints need security groups and optional private DNS; Gateway endpoints do not use security groups.
Add Gateway S3 + Interface STS/Secrets endpoints in Lambda-in-VPC before blaming NAT for latency.
60s: Gateway for S3/DynamoDB (free, route table). Interface for everything else (ENI, SG, hourly). Endpoint policies restrict scope. Private DNS keeps SDK hostnames.
Follow-up: how do endpoint policies differ from IAM and security groups?
commonPitfalls: Saying VPC endpoints replace security groups gets you rejected — Gateway has no ENI SG; Interface still needs tcp/443 rules.
Strong answer: Gateway = route target; Interface = ENI + SG + endpoint policy + optional private DNS.
Using Interface endpoint type for S3 — S3 uses Gateway endpoints.
Forgetting to associate all private route tables with the Gateway endpoint.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node SDK uses regional hostnames; VPC private DNS redirects resolution inside the VPC without code changes.
TypeScript Lambdas in VPC need endpoints or NAT for AWS API calls — similar to corporate proxy NO_PROXY lists.
